newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 4.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- ALLIANCE AND LEICESTER SAVERS IN REVOLT OVER FLOAT TERMS

A group headed by one of the Alliance and Leicester Building Society's former agents, Patrick Mountain, threatens to revolt the group's plans for a 2.8 billion stg floatation. He said he will consider requisitioning a special meeting of the action group so that he and other members can have their views heard by the society's board. He also said members will withdraw most of their savings. Members are angry over the decision to give 250 shares to each of its 2.4 million members regardless of how much money they have invested.
-- NORTHERN RULES OUT APPEAL FOR MERGERS PROBE

Northern Electric has decided not to lobby for a Monopolies Commission inquiry into the 766 million stg hostile bid from the American power group CalEnergy. The utility will not challenge the bidder on anything other than price, despite concerns over the US group's financial strength. CalEnergy looked likely to face close regulatory scrutiny as the company has yet to satisfy the City and regulators that its debt-ridden balance sheet is strong enough to support a takeover.
-- CO-OP CHIEF SEES TOUGH CHALLENGE

Graham Melmoth is set to takeover as head of the Co- operative Wholesale Society, the finance, food and funerals group. The three million stg business is the largest Co-operative organisation in Europe. Melmoth said the group has shown that it can renew itself to adapt to new circumstances and that the group will live up to the principles of honesty, openness, social responsibility and caring for others into the next century.
THE TIMES
-- BT SEALS $20 BLN TAKEOVER OF MCI TO BECOME GLOBAL FORCE

Chief executive of British Telecom, Sir Peter Bonfield, has described a $20 billion takeover of the US telecommunications group MCI as the largest transatlantic deal in history and will create a high-growth, global communications powerhouse. He said the deal would raise BT's earnings after one year and would add 500 million stg a year to combined pre-tax profits after five years. The two companies are merging their operations to form a holding company called Concert.
-- IOD SURVEY SHOWS FALL IN BUSINESS CONFIDENCE

According to evidence from the Institute of Directors, business confidence is falling significantly even though there is continuing improvement in the economy, with increases in orders, profits and overall company performances. Directors say that improvements in manufacturing are flattening out and overall uncertainty is leading them to reinforce calls to Chancellor Kenneth Clarke to present a cautious budget on November 26.
-- MCCAIN CHIPS IN WITH THE LOTTERY

The privately-owned Canadian company McCain has signed a deal with National Lottery operator Camelot which will allow them to use the lottery name, slogans and logo for promotions. This is part of Camelot's plan to set up a series of cross-promotional marketing partnerships with companies in different consumer sectors. McCain paid an undisclosed sum to Camelot and plans to spend five million stg on a series of campaigns.
THE GUARDIAN
-- SHAREHOLDERS EXPECTED TO RECEIVE DOUBLE BONUS

City analysts forecast that an offer of a 35 pence-per-share dividend to BT investors will send shares in the group soaring and will provide a boost for the London market generally. The attraction of BT becoming part of the world's second biggest telecoms company would boost shares, giving investors a double bonus. Telecoms analyst at broker HSBC James Capel, Martin
Mabbutt, said that BT would be given the thumbs up by the City.
-- PO GIVES PACKAGE TO RED STAR

The rail parcels business sold by the Government for one pound stg, Red Star, has signed a deal with the Post Office to carry parcels and same-day mail packages. PO played down the deal saying the amounts involved were only a fraction of the daily items sent by rail and road. Red Star have refused to comment about the contract but confirmed it was an extension of a pre-privatisation agreement.
-- LONDON TRANSPORT STILL EUROPE'S NUMBER ONE

According to a poll of 500 top European businesses by Healey and Baker, the property giants, London's public transport system is the best in Europe. London has been top of the poll for several years running, followed by Paris, Frankfurt and Brussels. London was voted number one for internal transport by 26 percent of respondents. London was also rated as being highly polluted and likely to lose its top position as a commercial centre to Frankfurt should Britain not participate in the single currency.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- OPEN SKIES BATTLE TO BE RENEWED

In the bid to break the deadlock over an open skies agreement across the Atlantic, British and US negotiators have decided to begin a fresh round of talks. The plan is to open up Heathrow to all US carriers and is vital if British Airways and American Airlines are to get a go-ahead for their alliance. Industry insiders believe it may be difficult for the two sets of negotiators to make headway over the issues that separate them.
-- UNIONS START CAMPAIGN FOR RECOGNITION

Laws planned by the Labour Party has led employees' leaders to target companies to persuade them to reorganise their unions. ISTC, the main steel union in partnership with other TUC affiliates, will begin the campaign with Johnson Matthey of north London and Co-Steel, the Canadian company. Both companies have withdrawn recognition from unions but have said they may reverse this if Labour is elected in the next general election. Other unions are expected to adopt a similar strategy.
-- US GIANT WILL FIGHT 13 BILLION STG BT TAKEOVER

The largest telecommunications company in the US, AT&T, has made it clear it will fight BT's takeover of MCI. AT&T is preparing a formal complaint to the US regulator, the Federal Communications Commission, claiming the takeover should be prevented on the grounds that other US operators do not have free access to British markets. Under US law, BT must get the FCC's agreement to increase its stake in MCI above 25 percent.
